---
title: "Foundation Model"
description: "A broadly pretrained model that can be adapted to many downstream tasks."
term: "Foundation Model"
letter: "F"
category: "Generative AI"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A foundation model is a model trained on broad data that can serve as a
starting point for many applications. It may be used directly, prompted,
fine-tuned, or combined with tools and external data.

## Technical explanation

Foundation models are typically large models pretrained with self-
supervised or other broad objectives on diverse data. Their capabilities
and limitations depend on training data, architecture, post-training, and
evaluation. The term describes a role and training approach, not one
specific model architecture.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Starting from a foundation model can reduce the need to train from
scratch and support many tasks. Engineers must still assess task fit,
licensing, data governance, cost, latency, safety, and whether adaptation
is needed.

## How it works

A model is pretrained on broad data to learn general representations or
generation behaviour. Downstream applications use it through prompting,
additional training, retrieval, or integration with other components.
Each deployment should be evaluated for its own task and users.

## Practical example

A pretrained vision model can be adapted to identify a specialized set
of manufacturing defects using a smaller task-specific dataset.

## Common misconceptions

- A foundation model is not automatically general-purpose, reliable, or
  safe for every task.
- Pretraining data and model capabilities may be incompletely documented.
- Using a foundation model does not remove the need for application-level
  evaluation and safeguards.
